item: A dead Wikipedia stream is restarted, Start and Run-now resume the lane, the drain loop keeps trying, and the soak window says why a lane is quiet
status: shipped (fixture-verified; awaiting the operator's next bundle)
key_paths: src/wiki/runner.py; src/wiki/service.py; src/monitoring/release_run.py; src/api/scheduler.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; tests/test_wiki_lane_supervisor.py; tests/test_wiki_runner.py; tests/test_wiki_drain_bound.py; tests/test_wiki_counters.py
summary: Read from the 15 diagnostics bundles of 2026-10-06: two lanes went quiet for days (hP from 10-04 08:07, NUC from 09-30) because the stream thread ended for good on a refused reconnect and the drain loop ended for good after 3 failed drains. revive_stream restarts a dead stream before each drain; start_wiki_lane revives or rebuilds the lane and is now also called by /api/scheduler/start and /run-now; failed drains wait 30 s growing to a 300 s ceiling (FAILING_RETRY_CEILING_S, which protects how long a recovered lane sits idle and how long the single writer is left alone) and the status reports degraded and retry_in_s; stop_wiki_lane joins outside the lock; the soak-window lane block carries the service state, and a zero-byte lane file reads as never stored anything. 21 new tests, mutation-checked.
